items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
PHP-IDS-26-001, Infectious Diseases Report
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Medical Officer of Health, provided an update on infectious disease trends in the Region and on Public Health's response to changing community needs and growing service pressures. She highlighted that case contact management by Public Health plays a crucial role in managing the spread of disease.

Dr. Wang noted that there has been an increase in diseases that require prolonged follow up, and effective management of these cases requires significant staff time and other resources. She also noted that there have been increasing barriers to infectious disease testing, treatment, and ongoing care, including limited access to primary care, housing instability, and other social or economic challenges. As a result, Public Health is often required to take a more hands-on approach to support these individuals.

Dr. Wang explained that infectious disease activity can shift quickly, which requires Public Health to remain ready to respond to these situations rapidly while maintaining service continuity of other programs and services. This requires moving to a more integrated model of disease management that allows greater flexibility and makes better use of available capacity across the organization. She also noted that the infectious disease surge response plan is being updated, which will strengthen preparedness for future pressures and support a coordinated response to disease surge scenarios.

In response to the Committee, Dr. Wang indicated that while additional staff resources are always beneficial, structural changes and reorganization have strengthened Public Health's ability to respond to community needs effectively with existing staff resources.

David Aoki, Director, Infectious Disease, highlighted that structural updates, including integrating teams and diversifying staff skill sets, have helped to strengthen resilience and capacity by enabling increased flexibility to shift resources as needed.

The Committee commended Public Health's efforts in significantly reducing numbers of unvaccinated school pupils.

N. Salonen joined the meeting at 9:20 a.m. 

In response to the Committee, D. Aoki emphasized the importance of emergency response planning efforts and preparedness in building organizational resilience and adaptability. Dr. Wang also emphasized coordination with healthcare partners to ensure system readiness for any emerging threats.

Dr. Wang noted that the approach and protocols for tick testing in Ontario and Canada have moved to the latest diagnostic testing methods. She recommended that individuals spending time in areas where ticks are likely to be found should check their bodies for ticks and tick bites, noting that instructions for tick removal are available on the Public Health website. She noted that individuals can visit etick.ca to submit tick photos for identification, also mentioning that tick exposure does not necessarily mean that an individual is at high risk for Lyme disease but that any concerns should be discussed with a primary care provider.

In response to questions from the Committee, Dr. Wang indicated that although wastewater monitoring was a useful tool to monitor Covid-19, the re-implementation of wastewater monitoring would not be necessary to inform or impact Public Health responses to infectious diseases at this time. She also noted that there is ongoing research regarding the detection of other infectious diseases in wastewater and that Public Health is monitoring this research and evidence.

Received for information.
